name: What are the most common mistakes on side-house additions?

mainEntity.name: What are the most common mistakes on side-house additions?
mainEntity.text: What are the most common mistakes on side-house additions?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common mistakes on side-house additions are surprisingly practical. Homeowners often focus on the new room itself and overlook setbacks, fire separation, drainage, roof tie-in, and how crews will actually build in the tight side yard. Another frequent problem is underestimating the amount of structural work needed to connect the addition to the existing house. Poor planning for windows, eaves, HVAC, and utility relocation can also lead to expensive redesigns. Some projects fail because the addition looks good in concept but does not fit the lot once measured accurately. Weak permit documentation is another big issue, because incomplete drawings often produce corrections and delays. The best way to avoid these mistakes is to verify the buildable envelope first, then design within it, and only then move to engineering and permit submittal. Side additions are very doable, but they reward careful planning and punish assumptions.
acceptedAnswer.description: The most common mistakes are ignoring setbacks, underestimating structural work, failing to plan for drainage and access, and choosing a design that looks good on paper but does not fit the lot. Weak permit documentation is another major cause of delays.
